slot.brief: Circuit of a cell with a resistor across which a voltmeter of given resistance is connected; find the voltmeter reading and the error caused by its finite resistance.

stem: In the circuit shown in the figure, a voltmeter of resistance $60\ \Omega$ is connected across a $15\ \Omega$ resistor. The cell has an emf of $30\ \text{V}$ and an internal resistance of $3\ \Omega$. The reading of the voltmeter and the absolute error caused by its finite resistance are, respectively:

verdicts.working: With voltmeter: 15||60 = 12 Ω; total = 12+3 = 15 Ω; reading = 30×12/15 = 24 V. Ideal (no voltmeter): V = 30×15/18 = 25 V. Absolute error = 25−24 = 1 V.

working:
1. True potential difference across $R = 15\ \Omega$ without the voltmeter:
The current in the unloaded circuit is:
$$I_0 = \dfrac{E}{R + r} = \dfrac{30}{15 + 3} = \dfrac{5}{3}\ \text{A}$$
The true potential difference is:
$$V_0 = I_0 R = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) \times 15 = 25\ \text{V}$$

2. Potential difference with the voltmeter connected:
The parallel equivalent resistance of the resistor and the voltmeter is:
$$R_p = \dfrac{R \cdot R_V}{R + R_V} = \dfrac{15 \times 60}{15 + 60} = \dfrac{900}{75} = 12\ \Omega$$
The total equivalent resistance of the circuit becomes:
$$R_{\text{eq}} = R_p + r = 12 + 3 = 15\ \Omega$$
The current drawn from the cell is:
$$I = \dfrac{E}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{30}{15} = 2\ \text{A}$$
The voltmeter reading is the potential difference across $R_p$:
$$V = I R_p = 2 \times 12 = 24\ \text{V}$$

3. Absolute error in measurement:
$$\Delta V = |V_0 - V| = |25 - 24| = 1\ \text{V}$$

Thus, the reading is $24\ \text{V}$ and the error is $1\ \text{V}$.

Independent check: With voltmeter: 15||60 = 12 Ω; total = 12+3 = 15 Ω; reading = 30×12/15 = 24 V. Ideal (no voltmeter): V = 30×15/18 = 25 V. Absolute error = 25−24 = 1 V.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A assumes that the total circuit current remains unchanged at $5/3\ \text{A}$ after connecting the voltmeter, yielding $V = (5/3) \times 12 = 20\ \text{V}$ and an error of $25 - 20 = 5\ \text{V}$.

Option D assumes an ideal voltmeter ($R_V \to \infty$), resulting in the unloaded reading of $25\ \text{V}$ and zero error.

figure.description: A rectangular single-loop circuit diagram with one parallel branch. The top horizontal segment contains a DC cell labeled '30 V' (positive terminal on the left indicated by a longer vertical line, negative on the right) in series with a resistor labeled 'r = 3 \Omega'. The right vertical branch contains a resistor labeled 'R = 15 \Omega'. Connected across this 15 \Omega resistor between two junction nodes above and below it is an outer parallel branch containing a voltmeter represented as a circle with the letter 'V' inside, labeled 'R_V = 60 \Omega'. The bottom horizontal wire connects the lower junction back to the cell's negative terminal.
